h1:
Khon Kaen to Chaiyaphum, 3 Days 2 Nights
Siam Tulip Fields + Waterfalls
intro: Khon Kaen and Chaiyaphum sit closer together than most people realise. A drive of just about two hours swaps the buzz of an Isan city for rainy-season hills covered in pink Siam tulips blooming right across the ridgelines. This is a 3-day, 2-night plan built for an easy self-drive with no need to rush, taking in the flower fields, the waterfalls, and Mo Hin Khao, the rock formation locals have nicknamed Thailand's Stonehenge.

blocks.html: Chaiyaphum is where people from Khon Kaen like to slip away during the rainy season, because June through August is exactly when the Siam tulips bloom. Pink fields stretch as far as you can see along the Phang Hoei ridge, a sight you only get to catch once a year. Add in waterfalls running at full strength in the wet months and it becomes a cross-province trip that more than earns its fuel cost. We've built this plan to start from Khon Kaen, drive yourself, and stay two nights in Chaiyaphum town.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Siam tulips bloom according to each year's rainfall, so before you go it's worth calling ahead to check the bloom percentage with Pa Hin Ngam National Park (find their page as Pa Hin Ngam National Park) or Sai Thong (089 282 3437). That way you won't be disappointed. The peak, when the fields are full of flowers, runs from late June to mid-August.

From Khon Kaen town to Chaiyaphum town is roughly 110–125 kilometres, taking Highway 12 then 201, an easy drive of about two hours on good roads the whole way. We'd suggest renting a car or driving your own, because the main sights like the Siam tulip fields and the waterfalls sit outside town where public transport simply doesn't reach.

items: Day 1 — Leave Khon Kaen in the morning, reach Chaiyaphum by midday, visit Tat Ton Waterfall near town, then check in to your in-town hotel.
Day 2 — The main day of the trip: hit the Siam tulip fields at Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong, and catch the cliff-edge viewpoints.
Day 3 — Stop by Mo Hin Khao, Thailand's Stonehenge, then drive back to Khon Kaen.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Khon Kaen to Chaiyaphum + Tat Ton Waterfall

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Hit the road + a waterfall near town

items.activity: Leave Khon Kaen town, fill up the tank
items.note: Take Highway 12 → 201 heading for Chaiyaphum, around 110–125 km.

items.activity: Arrive in Chaiyaphum town, check in and drop your bags
items.note: Rooms in Chaiyaphum town start around 500–900 THB a night, easy to find along Haruethai Road and around the Chao Pho Phaya Lae monument.

items.activity: Lunch in town, try jaew hon hot pot or Isan food
items.note: Suan Ahan Tak Mok is known for its jaew hon and butter-grilled meats, open 11.00–23.00.

items.activity: Drive to Tat Ton Waterfall in Tat Ton National Park, about 21 km from town
items.note: Entry is 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children, 30 THB per car, open from morning to evening.

items.activity: Wander and splash around Tat Ton Waterfall, with a wide rock shelf you can walk across
items.note: In the rainy season the water runs full and beautiful. The falls are about 6 metres high and 50 metres wide, roughly a 200-metre walk in from the car park.

items.activity: Head back into town and rest
items.note: Save your energy for taking on the Siam tulip fields the next day.

items.activity: Dinner in Chaiyaphum town + a stroll to walk it off
items.note: Na Yai Bai does Isan fusion, with a standout grilled pork-neck salad, averaging 100–350 THB, open until 22.00.

blocks.title: On rainy-season waterfalls
blocks.html: In the wet season the rocks around the falls get very slippery, so wear shoes with good grip, don't walk on mossy stones, and if heavy rain makes the water rise fast, get out of the water straight away. Safety comes before a good photo.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Siam tulip fields at Pa Hin Ngam + Sai Thong

blocks.html: This is the main day of the trip. The Siam tulip fields lie out toward Thep Sathit and Nong Bua Rawe districts, a fair distance from Chaiyaphum town, about 1.5–2 hours of driving. Set off early to beat the midday heat and catch the best light. The Siam tulips come in pink (bua sawan) and white (bua thep apsorn), and bloom across the fields from late June to mid-August.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Taking on two national parks of Siam tulips

items.activity: Leave the hotel early, grab breakfast to eat in the car on the way
items.note: The earlier you go, the fresher the flowers, the softer the light, and the fewer the crowds.

items.activity: Reach Pa Hin Ngam National Park in Thep Sathit and see the Siam tulip fields
items.note: Entry is 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children, 30 THB per car, open 06.00–18.00. There's a tram up to the fields for 30 THB per person.

items.activity: Walk the Siam tulip fields, the Lan Hin Ngam rock plain, and the Sut Phaendin viewpoint
items.note: Lan Hin Ngam is a field of oddly shaped rocks carved by erosion, within the same park and an easy walk on from the flowers.

items.activity: Drive on to Sai Thong National Park in Nong Bua Rawe
items.note: Sai Thong has 5 big tulip fields along the Phang Hoei ridge. Entry is 40 THB.

items.activity: Lunch at the park restaurant or from what you've packed
items.note: The park has a restaurant and visitor rest areas.

items.activity: Walk out to Pha Ham Hot and Pha Pho Mueang, with lovely cliff-edge viewpoints
items.note: Pha Ham Hot is a slab of rock jutting out over the cliff edge, great for photos, but take care because it's high and there's no solid railing.

items.activity: Take your last shots, then drive back to Chaiyaphum town
items.note: The return takes about 1.5–2 hours. Leave before dark, since the mountain roads have no lighting.

items.activity: Dinner in town and rest up for your last night
items.note: Comehome is a warm, cosy restaurant and cafe with à la carte dishes, steaks, and Isan food, open 10.30–20.30, closed Mondays.

blocks.title: Pa Hin Ngam vs Sai Thong, which to pick
blocks.html: If you're short on time, go with Pa Hin Ngam, since it bundles the Siam tulip fields, the Lan Hin Ngam rock plain, and the Sut Phaendin viewpoint into one spot, with easier walking. Sai Thong has wider fields and the standout cliff-edge view from Pha Ham Hot, but involves more walking. If you commit a full day, you can do both, as in this plan.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Mo Hin Khao, then back to Khon Kaen

blocks.html: On the last day, stop by Mo Hin Khao in Phu Laen Kha National Park, a cluster of white sandstone pillars standing across a wide plain that earned it the nickname Thailand's Stonehenge. It's out toward Mueang Chaiyaphum district, not too far from town, so you can see it in the morning and drive back to Khon Kaen in the afternoon, timed just right.

items.activity: Pack up, check out, have breakfast
items.note: You can leave your bags in the car, plan to see Mo Hin Khao and then head straight home.

items.activity: Drive to Mo Hin Khao in Phu Laen Kha National Park, Tha Hin Ngom subdistrict
items.note: Open 07.00–18.00, entry around 30–50 THB per person. The final stretch up the mountain is narrow, so drive carefully.

items.activity: Walk among the 5 stone pillars and the Mo Hin Khao rock plain
items.note: The largest pillar stands about 12 metres tall, white sandstone in odd shapes, best photographed in the morning's angled light.

items.activity: Come down from the mountain, have lunch in Chaiyaphum town before heading back
items.note: Good time to pick up gifts too, with Korat-style mee noodles and Chaiyaphum silk easy to find in town.

items.activity: Set off back to Khon Kaen
items.note: Take the same route, 201 → 12, about 2 hours, reaching Khon Kaen in the late afternoon.

items.activity: Arrive in Khon Kaen, trip done
items.note: If you've still got energy, round it off with dinner around Bueng Kaen Nakhon.

blocks.html: This budget assumes 2–4 people driving together and splitting costs, and doesn't include car rental. The figures are estimates to make planning easier, and real prices depend on the season and the hotel you pick.

items: Entry to 3 parks — around 120–150 THB per person total (Tat Ton + Pa Hin Ngam/Sai Thong + Phu Laen Kha)
Hotel, 2 nights — from 500–900 THB a night, cheaper once split
Food — 80–200 THB per meal, 3 meals a day
Fuel + tolls — round trip Khon Kaen–Chaiyaphum plus driving within the province, around 800–1,200 THB per car

blocks.html: The heart of this trip is the Siam tulips, which only bloom in the rainy season. Miss this window and you'll see nothing but green meadows with no flowers, so timing matters a lot.

items: Late June–mid-August — the peak, when the fields are at their fullest and prettiest, but also the busiest and rainiest
Early June — flowers starting to open, still few crowds, a relaxed feel
September — late season, flowers fading, though Sai Thong still has some to see through mid-month
Outside the rainy season — no Siam tulips, but Tat Ton Waterfall and Mo Hin Khao are open year-round

blocks.title: Straight from us
blocks.html: The Siam tulip fields really are lovely, but don't expect a dense carpet of pink like in the promo shots every single time, because how thick the blooms are depends on that year's rainfall. Some years there are fewer flowers, and in spots the white blooms mix in with the pink. Calling ahead to check the bloom percentage before you set off helps you avoid disappointment, and be ready for the chance of rain while you're out walking the fields.

faq.q: Is Chaiyaphum far from Khon Kaen, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Not far. It's roughly 110–125 kilometres, about a two-hour drive via Highway 12 then 201 on good roads the whole way. It works fine as a self-drive day trip or as an overnight stay.

faq.q: What month do the Chaiyaphum Siam tulips bloom?
faq.a: Siam tulips bloom in the rainy season, roughly June through mid-September, with the fullest and prettiest fields from late June to mid-August. Before you go, call the park to check what percentage is in bloom.

faq.q: What's the difference between the Siam tulip fields at Pa Hin Ngam and Sai Thong?
faq.a: Pa Hin Ngam in Thep Sathit district bundles the Siam tulip fields, the Lan Hin Ngam rock plain, and the Sut Phaendin viewpoint into one spot, with easy walking and a tram service. Sai Thong in Nong Bua Rawe has up to 5 wide fields and the cliff-edge view at Pha Ham Hot, but involves more walking. With time, you can do both in one day.

faq.q: How much is entry to each park?
faq.a: Parks in Chaiyaphum charge Thai adults around 40 THB, children 20 THB, and about 30 THB per car. Some, like Phu Laen Kha, may run 30–50 THB per person. Pa Hin Ngam adds a 30 THB tram up to the fields.

faq.q: Do you need your own car, or can you go by public transport?
faq.a: We'd recommend driving your own car or renting one for this trip, because the Siam tulip fields and waterfalls sit outside town and are spread across several districts, where public transport doesn't reach the main sights. If you don't have a car, you can hire a van with a driver from Chaiyaphum or Khon Kaen town.
